newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice trade modest, Iraq developments watched.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice trade modest, Iraq developments watched.

text.p: The easing baht barely benefited Thailand's FOB rice market this week as tighter paddy supplies kept prices steady to firmer this week, trade sources said on Thursday.
Trading volume was modest. Some in the market shifted attention to developments in Iraq, hoping that Baghdad would buy more rice from Thailand if it was allowed to resume limited crude oil exports.
"Iraq emerged a very strong buyer this year. We want to see that trend continue," said a commerce ministry official in charge of rice trade.
Iraq has bought 390,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand so far this year, 300,000 tonnes of which were outside the United Nations' oil-for-food programme.

"During the first quarter of this year alone, rice exports to Iraq fetched more than 300 million baht while rice trade with Iraq for the whole of 1995 was worth only 35 million baht," the official said.
There was not much fresh buying in the FOB market this week. Activities were limited mostly to buying in the domestic market to cover contracts.
"Prices remained high and that kept buyers on the sideline. The overall demand was sluggish," said a Bangkok trader.
Tight supplies at the end of the season offset the benefit of a weakened baht. But more supplies were expected to enter the market by the end of next month.
Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade edged up to $330-345 per tonne FOB Bangkok while 100 percent fragrant rice was barely change at $700-720 per tonne on the same basis.
Thailand has so far exported 2.45 million tonnes of rice this year.
